starting-off-talking-to-ellamaria.player: What's going on here? I see a lot of farming patches with nothing growing in them.

starting-off-talking-to-ellamaria.player: One? I'm not sure I understand you-

starting-off-talking-to-ellamaria.player: Well for a moment there I thought there was a dog around here somewhere...

starting-off-talking-to-ellamaria.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
starting-off-talking-to-ellamaria.text: Oh yes, sarcasm - how amusing. No, no, peasant - I have a question to ask of you, and you are required to answer.

starting-off-talking-to-ellamaria.player: Well, seeing as you put it so nicely...

steps.text: Ah, more sarcasm - wonderful. Well, it is nice to have a master of the fine art of gardening to assist me; in the absence of any such person, I gladly accept your service.

steps.player: I'm not sure if that's a compliment or not. Anyway, what would you like me to do, and what do I get out of it?

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: To answer your first question, you have noticed the new farming patches that we have had installed around us. We wish to grow many varied and exotic plants in them, to bring happiness back to my husband.

steps.player: King Roald?

steps.text: The very same, and that's 'His Most Royal Majesty' to you. Now we come to the plants that one wishes you to grow in these patches. I would tell you all at once, but I fear that your small mind would not cope.

steps.player: Thanks, I'm sure. So tell me Queeny, how do I know which plants I am to get for you?

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: I have given you a list of the items that I need in each patch. One is sure that you will know how to use the list with each patch to find out what needs to go in each one. There is one more thing, though.

steps.player: One listens with bated breath...

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Obtaining the seeds may prove difficult if you go about it by hacking and slashing everything that moves. No, to gather these items you will need to employ a finer tactic; the art of persuasion.

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: You must go at once and converse with the wise old man who is said to dwell in Draynor Village; he may guide you in mastering this delicate and sophisticated ability.

options.text: No.

steps.player: I'd rather jump off the docks at Port Sarim.

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Well don't allow one to delay you - it is probably the most constructive thing you could do with your life, to be honest.

steps.player: You know Queen Ellamaria?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Oh yes, we go way back, long before she married that fool the King of Varrock. She wasn't always royal you know.

steps.player: Really?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: No, in her youth she was a barmaid at the Blue Moon inn. All that fancy talk, that's just for show. No, the Ellamaria I knew was as common as muck, until she lucked onto good King Roald.

steps.player: I'll certainly look at her in a different light when I return to Varrock.

steps.text: So what sort of guidance has Little-Miss-Hoity-Toity sent you to seek?

steps.player: I am supposed to gain some knowledge of diplomacy and persuasion from you.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: That is an area that - luckily for you, young [player name] - I have studied. Have you heard of the diplomat known as Charos?

steps.player: Charos? I must say the name rings a bell...
Charos...
Yes, I remember! Once, during my travels to Morytania, I came upon an item of magical jewellery called the Ring of Charos.

steps.text: If everything I have heard about Charos's ring is true, it will not stay lost forever. Where did you originally find it?

steps.text: In order to find the ring it may be wise to return to Fenkenstrain - he may have found a way to regain it. If you manage to reobtain the ring, return to me and I will reveal its secrets to you.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Charos rose to power under the rule of Lord Drakan of Morytania, his only living servant. The Vampyre Lord suffered the existence of Charos because of the talents that this sophisticated diplomat had to offer.

steps.player: The art of persuasion?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Indeed. Charos had many uses - spy, assassin, negotiator - because he could convince anyone to do his wishes. These talents were in some part Charos's own, but greatly enhanced by the ring that he fashioned.

steps.player: The Ring of Charos.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Exactly. One who wears the ring must possess some innate ability of their own, which the ring enhances so that the wearer can convince all but the most strong- minded to do their bidding.

steps.player: What happened to Charos? And why did Fenkenstrain have the ring?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Charos had a castle built on the northern coast of Morytania, where he dwelt for many years in service to Drakan. None really know what became of him, but some say that he became too certain of his abilities,

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: and turned them on his master. This would have been his ultimate downfall, for the ring's power would have had little or no effect upon Drakan.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Fenkenstrain probably found the ring many years later, buried somewhere within the depths of Charos's castle.

steps.player: So what you are telling me is that nobody really knows what happened to Charos? That he could still be alive? And if he is still alive...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: ...he would naturally come looking for the ring that is his by right. But I don't believe that you should worry about that - it has been many years since his disappearance, and the likelyhood is that he is dead.

steps.player: Still - it doesn't inspire me with much confidence.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I could activate the power within this ring for you, but for me to do that I must know that you will use it wisely. To do that I must ask you a few questions, to see how good a diplomat you can be.

steps.player: Okay, go ahead...

steps.text: Note that the answers are randomly shuffled; Answer A may switch to C/B if retaking the test.

1/7: Two goblins are fighting over the colour of their armour. What do you do?[A] Kill them both and steal their bronze spears.[B] Leave them to it. Armour's not going to help - any noob could take them.[C] Show them a range of colours so that they can come to a compromise.

2/7: A Drunken dwarf offers you a kebab. What do you do?[A] Take his generous gift even though you have no need for it.[B] Run away leaving the lonely dwarf on his own.[C] Stand there until he gets annoyed and attacks you.
3/7: Are you enjoying your experience of Farming?[A] Definitely.[B] Yes.[C] It's absolutely, unquestionably the most interesting thing I've ever done!

4/7: A dwarf asks you to put on a silly golden helmet so that you can be fired from a cannon into a wall. What do you do?[A] Refuse this crazy request blankly.[B] Put on the silly helmet and jump into the cannon.[C] Put the helmet on the dwarf and fire him into the wall.

5/7: You meet Pkmaster0036 in the wilderness who asks you who is the greatest player killer in the world. How do you answer?[A] Cower in fear and quickly cast teleport to Varrock.[B] You of course Pkmaster0036, no one could ever challenge your greatness![C] I am, prepare to meet your doom Pkmaster0036!

What do you say?[A] No, especially not that wise old man, who doesn't look at all suspicious.[B] If I do I'll let you know.[C] Yes, that wise old man over there looks incredibly dodgy.

steps.text: It is but the smallest of our worries. We get by, we survive, on the miserable harvests that I grow here. The price of our survival is what pains me, as it is a price I have paid with the souls of others.

options.text: Ah, it all makes sense now - you're a psychopath.

steps.player: Ah, it all makes sense now - you're a psychopath.

options.text: [Charm] Whatever you've done, I'm sure you had just cause.

steps.speaker: Lyra
steps.text: You say this, but you know nothing of my crimes. I cannot tell you all, but this much I will say – that being allowed to exist in this land is a privilege that must be paid for, and the cost is dear.

options.text: Yawn* Could you get to the point please?

steps.speaker: Lyra
steps.text: If your time is so pressing then leave me be and go about your business!

options.text: [Charm] And what is the nature of this fee that you pay?

steps.player: And what is the nature of this fee that you pay?

steps.speaker: Lyra
steps.text: Mother and I must pay a tithe of blood to the vampyres. Father would have protected us, but he is no longer with us, although his presence still walks among us in the fields. We pay with the blood of others.

options.text: Er, can I withdraw my offer of help now?

steps.player: Er, can I withdraw my offer of help now?

options.text: [Charm] If not yours, then whose blood are you offering?

steps.player: If not yours, then whose blood are you offering?

steps.speaker: Lyra
steps.text: Sometimes I travel to market fairs in distant lands, and I use my feminine arts to lure young farmers back to this land; then the vampyres come for them and I see them no more.

options.text: Something tells me that you actually enjoy it, really.

steps.player: Something tells me that you actually enjoy it, really.

steps.speaker: Lyra
steps.text: I would not talk so if I were you - I know a secret call that will bring the vampyres here right now, and then you may live only long enough to feel regret for your impertinence.

options.text: [Charm] How can you deal with so much guilt?

steps.player: How can you deal with so much guilt?

steps.speaker: Lyra
steps.text: Please - ask me no more. You said that you were looking for some orchid seeds? I do have some as a matter of fact, and you may as well have them because they do not grow well in this grim land.

steps.player: Okay, can I have them then...

steps.speaker: Lyra
steps.text: You must pass a test first. These are no ordinary flowers, and no ordinary farmer can grow them. You must grow onions here in one of these patches, and when they are fully grown I will give you the seeds.

options.text: That's a deal - I'll grow a patch of onions for you.

steps.player: That's a deal – I'll grow a patch of onions for you.

steps.speaker: Lyra
steps.text: Speak to me when they are fully grown. You need not pick them for me, I will be able to assess your skills by simply watching you.

options.text: I think not - I've loitered too long in this land.

steps.player: I think not – I've loitered too long in this land.

steps.speaker: Lyra
steps.text: Yes, I agree - far too long.

options.text: [Charm] Oh for Saradomin's sake, just give me the seeds!

steps.player: Oh for Saradomin's sake, just give me the seeds!

steps.speaker: Lyra
steps.text: This feeling in my head - it is so strange - and it is a feeling I have felt before, although I cannot explain it. If you are trying to use some unnatural power over me, you have failed.

options.text: I can't take it anymore - just give me the seeds.

steps.text: And to think I listened to you! I was right after all - there is no kindness between human beings anymore.

options.text: [Charm] So what ails you, my friend?

steps.player: So what ails you, my friend?

options.text: Oh stop whining, it's not like you do it for free.

talking-to-bernald.speaker: Bernald
talking-to-bernald.text: Do you know anything about grapevine diseases?

talking-to-bernald.speaker: Bernald
talking-to-bernald.text: You see those grapevines over there?

talking-to-bernald.player: Yes. They don't look too happy at the moment.

talking-to-bernald.speaker: Bernald
talking-to-bernald.text: They've come down with some strange disease that I've never encountered before. I've tried everything with them, but nothing seems to work. If it carries on like this I will lose all this year's crops.

talking-to-bernald.player: I could probably help you with that, but I'd need something in return.

talking-to-bernald.speaker: Bernald
talking-to-bernald.text: Anything, you just need to ask!

talking-to-bernald.player: Well, I'd like a supply of Burthorpe Vine seeds.

talking-to-bernald.speaker: Bernald
talking-to-bernald.text: I'm afraid I can't do that.
If the player is not wearing the Ring of Charos:

steps.player: I thought you said anything!

steps.speaker: Bernald
steps.text: I'm afraid that is the one thing I cannot give you. Burthorpe Vine has been bred over many years and many past generations of my family. I could never give away something so special.

options.text: I thought you said anything!
[Charm] But it is the only way that these vines will be cured.

steps.player: But it is the only way that these vines will be cured.

steps.speaker: Bernald

options.text: I accept the deal.

steps.player: Actually, it seems like a lot of hard work for nothing.

steps.speaker: Bernald

talking-to-bernald-talking-to-bernald-af.speaker: Bernald
talking-to-bernald-talking-to-bernald-af.text: Plant cure not doing the trick, eh?

talking-to-bernald-talking-to-bernald-af.player: I don't understand - it's worked with everything else.

talking-to-bernald-talking-to-bernald-af.speaker: Bernald
talking-to-bernald-talking-to-bernald-af.text: That grapevine disease must be much stronger than the usual. You'll need something a bit more potent to cut out that infection.

talking-to-bernald-talking-to-bernald-af.player: Do you know of any stronger cures?

talking-to-bernald-talking-to-bernald-af.speaker: Bernald
talking-to-bernald-talking-to-bernald-af.text: No, I don't - but I know of a man who might. Not far from here there's a druid gardener who goes by the name of Alain. He's an expert on things like this, so they tell me.

talking-to-bernald-talking-to-bernald-af.player: Why didn't you just go and ask him yourself?

talking-to-bernald-talking-to-bernald-af.speaker: Bernald
talking-to-bernald-talking-to-bernald-af.text: These vines are very precious indeed. I could not hazard the risk that someone would steal my grapes while I was away - they may be diseased, but they still contain Burthorpe Vine seeds.

options.text: I need to ask you about strong plant cures.

steps.player: I need to ask you about strong plant cures.

steps.speaker: Alain
steps.text: Well, you have come to the right person, then - I researched exotic plant diseases as part of my druidic training. What is the affliction that you need to cure?

steps.player: Bernald up in Burthorpe has got some seriously diseased grapevines. I tried plant cure on them, but it didn't seem to have any positive effect.

steps.speaker: Alain
steps.text: Ah, so is this the famous Burthorpe Vine?

steps.player: The very one.

steps.speaker: Alain
steps.text: I'm afraid that my researches did not extend to Burthorpe Vine. Bernald and his ancestors have always closely guarded their heritage, that vine. In fact, I'm surprised that he has involved you.

steps.player: Er, I did have some ... assistance there.

steps.speaker: Alain
steps.text: I see. Well, if it involves some unnatural power I would rather not know. I prefer the use of power that can be brought forth from the plants around us.

options.text: Are you sure there's nothing you can suggest?

steps.player: Are you sure there's nothing you can suggest?

steps.speaker: Alain
steps.text: Well...

steps.speaker: Alain
steps.text: There is one thing you could try. One of the most potent cures I have discovered involves using the natural power held within a very special mineral, but it is a very closely guarded secret.

steps.player: Do you mean the rune essence?

steps.speaker: Alain
steps.text: You know of that?!? Then I can do no further harm here. You can make a potent plant cure by mixing some crumbled rune essence into a normal plant cure. This may possibly cure Bernald's vines.

steps.player: Thank you Alain, I will try it out immediately!

options.text: [Charm] You're hiding something from me.

steps.player: You're hiding something from me.

steps.speaker: Alain
steps.text: This is the power you are abusing!! I feel it now - it emanates from the ring you wear, a festering fountain of corruption that appalls my very soul!!!

steps.player: Oh, sorry. I forgot that it only works on the weak- minded.

options.text: You need to chill out and stop taking yourself so seriously.

steps.player: You need to chill out and stop taking yourself so seriously.

steps.speaker: Dantaera
steps.text: Leave me in peace then, if you are so unable to understand my grief.

options.text: [Charm] A secret is a dreadful burden to have to keep to yourself.

steps.player: A secret is a dreadful burden to have to keep to yourself.

steps.speaker: Dantaera
steps.text: It is not hard to keep this secret - to give it away would cause me great sorrow.

steps.player: I don't see how. Tell me your secret, and I will keep it as well as you have done.

steps.speaker: Dantaera
steps.text: Very well - I feel deep trust in you for some reason. It is the White Tree, last survivor of a race of Trees that have disappeared from our landscape. Once they covered the land; now there is only one.

steps.player: What happened to them?

options.text: You should get out a bit more and quit worrying about trees.

steps.text: Nothing interesting happens.

steps.player: (Hmmm ... better not let those guards see me...)

steps.text: So what are you doing this weekend?

If something is blocking the trolley:
The statue doesn't move.

The trolley moves 4 spaces away from the player.

The statue doesn't move.

talking-to-ellamaria-with-the-seeds.text: If the player uses the white tree sapling on Ellamaria:

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Very good peasant, thank you for showing one that, but one has given you a job to do. Do it.

talking-to-ellamaria-with-the-seeds.text: If the player uses the delphinium seeds on Ellamaria:

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Yes, very good peasant, you've got the seed; but it's delphiniums that one wishes, not seeds. Plant it in the delphinium patch, and let it grow.

talking-to-ellamaria-with-the-seeds.text: If the player uses either the pink or yellow orchid seeds on Ellamaria:

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Yes, very good peasant, you've got the seed; but it's orchids that one wishes, not seeds. Plant it in the orchid patch, and let it grow.

talking-to-ellamaria-with-the-seeds.text: If the player uses the vine seeds on Ellamaria:

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Yes, very good peasant, you've got the seed; but it's Burthorpe vine that one wishes, not seeds. Plant it in the Burthorpe vine patch, and let it grow.

talking-to-ellamaria-with-the-seeds.text: If the player uses the red/white/yellow rose seeds on Ellamaria:

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Yes, very good peasant, you've got the seed; but it's a [red/white/yellow] rosebush that one wishes, not seeds. Plant it in the [red/white/yellow] rosebush patch, and let it grow.

talking-to-ellamaria-with-the-seeds.text: If the player uses the snowdrop seeds on Ellamaria:

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Yes, very good peasant, you've got the seed; but it's snowdrops that one wishes, not seeds. Plant it in the snowdrop patch, and let it grow.

planting-the-seeds.text: If the player plants the seeds in the correct patch:

planting-the-seeds.text: If the player plants the seeds in the wrong patch:

steps.text: You can only plant those in the Varrock Palace garden.

planting-the-seeds.text: If the player attempts to use a watering can on the patches:

steps.text: These don't really need watering - the soil seems to be extremely fertile.

planting-the-seeds.text: If the player attempts to use regular/super/ultracompost on the patches:

steps.text: This patch doesn't really need treating with compost - the soil seems to be extremely fertile.

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Hey, why are you digging that up? Leave it alone!

steps.player: Oh, sorry, didn't mean to...

planting-the-seeds.text: If the player attempts to use a soil-filled plant pot on the plantpot:

planting-the-seeds.text: If the player attempts to use the seeds on the plantpot before adding compost first:

steps.text: This plantpot needs some compost in it first.

steps.text: These seeds need to be planted in the other plantpot.

planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.speaker: Ellamaria
planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.text: One finds that hard to believe. Out of my way, let me see for myself.

steps.text: Also, the [plant name] [hasn't/haven't] finished growing.

steps.text: Thirdly, the [plant name] [hasn't/haven't] finished growing.

steps.text: Oh look, the [plant name] [hasn't/haven't] finished growing.

steps.speaker: Ellamaria
steps.text: And what a surprise, the [plant name] [hasn't/haven't] finished growing.

planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.text: If seven patches haven't finished growing:

steps.speaker: Ellamaria
steps.text: Oh you are doing so well, the [plant name] [hasn't/haven't] finished growing.

steps.text: To add insult to injury, the [plant name] [hasn't/haven't] finished growing.

planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.text: If nine patches haven't finished growing:

steps.speaker: Ellamaria
steps.text: And finally, the [plant name] [hasn't/haven't] finished growing.

planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.speaker: Ellamaria
planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.text: One suggest you learn a little patience. These plants should not take long to grow - these patches have been filled with extremely fertile soil that was very expensive to import.
If all of the plants are fully grown and statues are placed on their plinths:

steps.speaker: Ellamaria
steps.text: Oh yes, very nice, if a little yobbish. Rollie will be so pleased–

steps.player: Rollie?!?

steps.speaker: Ellamaria
steps.text: You will address my husband by his proper title!!!!! Speaking of whom, I think it is time that we brought him to see his new garden. And when one says we, one means you.

steps.player: Oh, you want me to go and get Roald – sorry ... King Roald ... and bring him here. Fair enough, wait here then, I'll be back in a mo.

planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.speaker: Ellamaria
planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.text: So are you going to get Rollie then?

planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.player: No, I haven't spoken to Roll ... King Roald ... yet.

planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.speaker: Ellamaria
planting-the-seeds-talking-to-ellamaria-.text: Well hurry along peasant. This garden will be such a wonderful surprise!

talking-to-king-roald.speaker: King Roald
talking-to-king-roald.text: Yes, citizen. Do you need something?

options.text: Would you like to follow me for a minute?

steps.player: Would you like to follow me for a minute?

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Follow you?!? I am the King! I am the followed, not the follower!!
If the player is not wearing the Ring of Charos:

steps.player: Well, if you can't be bothered then neither can I.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Suit yourself.

steps.player: No, you suit yourself.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: You're quite argumentative for a peasant.

steps.text: Then why do you keep answering me back?

steps.player: No, you're answering me back.
Well, stop talking and I'll stop answering.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: No, you stop talking.

steps.player: I have stopped talking.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: No you haven't, you're doing it now.

steps.player: No, I'm just answering what you're saying.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Okay, so if I don't say anything, you won't answer me back.

steps.player: Suits me.

steps.text: Go on, then.

steps.player: No, you first.

steps.text: King Roald doesn't say anything to you.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: See, that's better.

steps.player: Yes, much better.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: What were you saying about me following you somewhere?

steps.player: I can't remember, it was such a long time ago.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Ah, that's a shame - I could have done with a breath of fresh air.

steps.player: Oh well.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Yes, never mind.

steps.player: See you around.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Yes, see you later.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: I thought you were going.

steps.player: I was until you spoke to me again.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: I'm sorry, I'll stop speaking to you then.

steps.player: See you around.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Yes, see you later.
If the player is wearing the Ring of Charos:

options.text: Well, if you can't be bothered then neither can I.
[Charm] Of course, your majesty - please forgive me.

steps.player: Of course, your majesty - please forgive me.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Forgiveness is something that cannot be earned so easily. And I'm certainly not following you off on some wild goose chase when I have important matters of state to attend to.

options.text: That's it - I've had it with royalty.

steps.player: That's it - I've had it with royalty.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: And I've had enough of peasantry! Get out of my castle!

options.text: [Charm] The Queen asked me to bring you.

steps.player: The Queen asked me to bring you.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Ellie?

steps.text: Now that's a different matter. Lead on, peasant - let's see what my darling wife has been up to now.

options.text: Not really.

steps.player: Not really.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: You will have to excuse me then. I am very busy as I have a kingdom to run!
